label: Flavoured tea and herbal infusions
about: Blended teas and caffeine-free herbal infusions sold as loose leaf, tea bags or iced blends. Tamil Nadu has the Nilgiris tea belt and the Coonoor auction close at hand.

Loose leaf pouches, tea bags, or iced blends?
Will you blend and pack yourself, or use a co-packer at first?
How many packs a month do you expect to sell in the first year?

regulatory.title: FSSAI registration or licence by turnover
regulatory.text: Basic registration up to ₹12 lakh annual turnover; State licence above that (up to ₹20 crore); Central licence above ₹20 crore. Apply on FoSCoS.

regulatory.title: 'Tea' only for products with tea leaves
regulatory.text: Blends with no Camellia sinensis leaf (e.g. mint hibiscus) should be labelled as an herbal or flower infusion, not as tea. FSSAI has issued an advisory on this — confirm the current wording before printing labels.

regulatory.title: Tea Board registration for tea blending or packing
regulatory.text: Businesses that buy, blend or pack tea may need registration with the Tea Board of India. Confirm whether your activity is covered.

regulatory.title: Legal Metrology declarations on packs
regulatory.text: Pre-packed goods carry mandatory declarations (name and address, net quantity, MRP, date, customer care); packers may need registration under the Packaged Commodities Rules.

regulatory.title: Trademark class 30
regulatory.text: Tea and tea-based beverages fall in Nice class 30; herbal infusions are commonly filed there too.
